evidence.quote: Strychnos spinosa is a seasonal fruit tree that is harvested between August and December
evidence.doc: Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)

harvestMonths.notes: SANBI PlantZAfrica gives only FLOWERING months for this species ('Produces small greenish-white flowers in dense heads at the ends of branches (Sep-Feb/Spring - summer)') and separately notes 'They take a long time to ripen', without giving a specific ripening/harvest month; the PMC8703348 review paper's Aug-Dec harvesting statement is used here as the actual harvest-month evidence instead.

evidence.quote: Presently, Strychnos spinosa can be propagated via seeds, grafting, or budding, with the production of fruit starting 3–5 years after planting
evidence.doc: Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)

evidence.quote: Fruit weighs between 145 and 383 g, while about 300–700 fruits (40–100 kg) can be produced per tree stand.
evidence.doc: Undervalued Spiny Monkey Orange (Strychnos spinosa Lam.): An Indigenous Fruit for Sustainable Food-Nutrition and Economic Prosperity (peer-reviewed review, PMC8703348)

yieldKgPerTreeMature.notes: Value taken directly as stated by the source in kg (40-100 kg per tree for 300-700 fruits); no conversion performed.

chillUnits.notes: No source states a chilling requirement or explicitly says the species has none.

pollination.notes: SANBI states only 'It is believed that various insects pollinate the flowers.' (Ecology section, https://pza.sanbi.org/strychnos-spinosa) -- this confirms insect pollination but does not state whether the species is self-fertile, partly-self-fertile, needs a cross-pollinator, or is dioecious, so no enum value could be confidently assigned. The ICRAF Agroforestree Database 4.0 fact sheet for this species (fetched PDF) contains a BOTANIC DESCRIPTION, ECOLOGY, PRODUCTS, TREE MANAGEMENT and GERMPLASM MANAGEMENT section but NO BIOLOGY section with reproductive/phenology detail, unlike the fact sheets for other species in this batch.
